uncited: This family encompasses techniques that generate volumetric data or manage rendering performance dynamically, rather than relying solely on static, pre-computed 3D textures.
It addresses the limitations of static data in terms of memory overhead, resolution limits, and interactivity.

The methods differ from standard direct volume ray casting by either computing density analytically via procedural noise functions (e.g., Worley noise) during the ray march [2447-volumetric-smoke-rendering-with-worley-noise-and-light-maps.md][8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md], applying spatial distortions to rays for focus+context [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md], modeling deformations via inverse displacement mapping [10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md], or dynamically selecting between multi-frame rate warping and parallel raycasting based on workload complexity [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].

The family shares the fundamental ray casting loop structure defined in [Direct volume ray casting](19-direct-volume-ray-casting.md), but modifies the sampling stage or the rendering pipeline control flow.

**Procedural Evaluation**: Instead of sampling a fixed 3D texture, density $V(\mathbf{p})$ is computed on-the-fly using mathematical functions (e.g., Fractal Brownian Motion, Worley noise) evaluated at the sample point $\mathbf{p}$ [8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md].

**Dynamic Ray Trajectories**: Rays may be distorted or redirected based on lens parameters or displacement fields, requiring custom intersection logic with the volume bounding box [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md][10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md].

**Adaptive Rendering**: The system may switch between rendering paradigms (e.g., image warping vs. full raycasting) based on runtime metrics like resolution and sampling rate [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].
The techniques originate from the need to render complex, dynamic volumetric phenomena (smoke, clouds) and interactive deformations that cannot be efficiently stored in static voxel grids.
Procedural noise methods leverage the parallelism of GPUs to compute density analytically [8240-procedural-volumetric-cloud-rendering-gpu-shader.md].
Lens techniques extend standard projection models to support interactive exploration [6767-gpu-accelerated-ray-casting-with-volumetric-lenses.md].
Displacement mapping adapts surface modeling concepts to volume data for interactive editing [10659-displacement-mapping-for-volume-rendering.md].
Multi-frame rate rendering addresses the performance bottlenecks of high-resolution raycasting in distributed or multi-GPU environments [11338-dynamic-multi-frame-rate-rendering.md].
